top_buyer_needs: Per-employee, per-device inventory of every AI agent, model, provider and MCP server actually used, including personal accounts, raw API keys, BYOK-in-IDE and local model runtimes that every vendor console admits it cannot see (47% lack an agent inventory; Zscaler 'basic inventory' gap).

Account identity per session: personal vs corporate vs API key vs Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, with a 'shadow account on corporate device' signal (58% of Claude use is personal; 67% of AI access on corporate devices uses non-corporate accounts).

Reconstructable agent action trail for 30+ days: tool calls, files read/written, shell commands, MCP servers, permission mode and approval source (46% of enterprises cannot produce one; 65% saw out-of-scope actions).
Secret/PII/source-code egress evidence without the monitoring tool storing prompt text: findings as fingerprint + class + session, never the value.
Detection of safeguards-disabled sessions (--dangerously-skip-permissions, YOLO, full-auto), destructive commands, sensitive-path reads and read-then-publish sequences.
MCP/hook/rules-file inventory with hash-based drift alerts and managed-allowlist comparison (MCPoison, Keyv worm, Agentjacking, OWASP MCP09).
Exact per-user/team/model/session token and cost attribution including subagents and cache economics, reconciled against vendor billing to find shadow spend.
No proxy in the request path, no base-URL rewrites, no latency, no hook fragility; coverage of subscription-auth agents gateways cannot see.

Privacy posture defensible to DPOs and works councils: metadata only, pseudonymous mode, retention cap, employee transparency screen, no performance scoring (GDPR 88, BetrVG, CNIL, WOR, Annex III 4(b)).
SIEM/SOAR-native export in standard shapes (OTLP gen_ai.*, Splunk HEC, syslog/webhook) reusing vendor event vocabularies so one rule set spans agents.
Policy-drift verification per endpoint (managed-settings.json, requirements.toml, Gemini system settings, enterprise hooks present) and agent version vs known-vulnerable floors.
Silent MDM deployment: signed/notarised pkg, published PPPC profile, ~50MB/1% CPU footprint, honest reduced-functionality state without FDA.

Audit evidence mapped to frameworks auditors already use (NIST AI 600-1, 800-53 AU/SI/AC, ISO 42001 A.6.2.8, SOC 2 CC6/CC7/CC9, OWASP ASI/MCP, ATLAS) with tamper-evident export and >=6-month retention.
Monitor-first, coach-not-block rollout with webhooks to an enforcement tool for phase two.
Predictable flat per-host pricing with a free tier, open-source endpoint code, SAML+SCIM, trust page and DPA before the first paid pilot.
feature_implications: Extract the fields Claude Code JSONL already carries but Vole discards (permissionMode, entrypoint, version, cwd, gitBranch, Bash input.command, hook_success/mcp_instructions_delta/failedMcpServers attachments) and Codex approval/sandbox/local_shell_call payloads; add per-version fixtures and a schema-drift incident.

Session identity classifier: org OAuth / personal OAuth / raw API key / Bedrock-Vertex-Foundry / ChatGPT workspace vs personal / Cursor team id, emitted as account_class on every session with a 'shadow account on corporate device' incident.

secret_sightings table: HMAC-SHA256 fingerprint (per-install Keychain key), detector id, provider, data class (secret|pci|phi|pii), confidence, tool, session, model, raw_ref offset, first/last seen, status; scanner runs in the JSONL tail before Claude Code's 30-day cleanup; rules from Betterleaks TOML; JWT decoded offline; verification opt-in only.

Scan agent-specific leak sinks repo scanners miss: .claude/settings.local.json allow-lists, MCP configs, hooks, spilled tool-output files, /share and feedback bundle writes, Gemini telemetry.log with logPrompts on, Goose llm_request.jsonl, Kiro globalStorage size.

Behaviour rule pack named after Anthropic's event vocabulary and tagged with OWASP ASI/MCP and ATLAS ids: permission_mode_escalation, bypass headless session, destructive command (rm -rf ~, force-push, DROP/DELETE, cloud deletes), sensitive-path read (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, .env, agent credential files), secret_then_publish, mcp_server_first_seen/changed, hook added in fresh clone, hidden-Unicode rules file, base-URL/proxy override, version below CVE floor.
Command-string classifier that persists only a pattern id and category (find -exec, xargs, sh -c, curl|sh, base64 pipelines, $IFS, long whitespace runs) independent of vendor allowlists.

MCP inventory per host and per session keyed by serverCommand/serverUrl (never serverName), diffed against managed allowlists, with tool-description hashes for rug-pull detection and privileged-credential tagging; export in server.json-compatible shape.

Endpoint inventory collectors needing no ES entitlement: installed AI apps via cask-derived bundle ids and ~/Library footprints; local model runtimes via listening ports 11434/1234/1337/4891 and manifest dirs (never conversation content); code-signing identity (TeamID/SigningID) per agent binary; unprivileged socket sampling tagged low-confidence.

Widen agents by payoff: Copilot CLI (~/.copilot session-state events.jsonl exact tokens), Gemini CLI chats, Goose sessions.db, Amp threads, Continue dev_data; activity-only with explicit 'no tokens' badge for Windsurf, Zed, Kiro, Cline/Roo, LM Studio/Jan/Ollama; honour CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Xcode sessions and dedupe Copilot Chat/CLI by session id.

Policy-posture report per endpoint: presence/hash of managed-settings.json, com.anthropic.claudecode MDM domain, GeminiCli system settings, ~/.codex requirements.toml, enterprise hooks.json; drift incident when observed behaviour contradicts policy.

Cost fields no vendor ships: session-grain tokens/cost with subagent roll-up, per-session tool attribution, cache-hit ratio, wrong-model-for-task heuristic; unit field for credits/seats; terminal/surface dimension.
Enterprise reconcile job against Anthropic usage_report, Cursor filtered-usage-events and Copilot NDJSON to surface unaccounted spend and shadow accounts.

OTLP/HTTP exporter (enterprise tier) emitting gen_ai.* metrics and invoke_agent/chat/execute_tool spans with provider.name, input/output_tokens, agent.name, conversation.id and never input/output.messages, pinned to a semconv snapshot; plus Splunk HEC, JSON/syslog/webhook; rows shaped on IETF draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 fields and carrying prompt.id/tool_use_id/traceparent for SIEM joins.
Optional localhost OTLP receiver and an optional tiny managed PreToolUse/beforeMCPExecution hook that only appends decisions to Vole's SQLite, keeping default install out of the request path.
Read-only local MCP server over Vole's SQLite so analysts' Claude Code/Codex sessions can query incidents and cost without any cloud.

Privacy Center screen and shipped data manifest (paths read, fields stored, exclusions, retention), pseudonymous enterprise mode with admin re-identification, retention cap default >=6 months, hard switch disabling per-person productivity views, works-council/CSE notice and DPIA template.

Tamper-evident evidence: hash-chained SQLite rows, signed exports, compliance pack mapped to NIST 600-1 action ids, 800-53 controls, ISO 42001 A.6.2.8, SOC 2 CC6/7/9, COSO metrics, AI-literacy per-user tool record.

Developer ID signing + notarisation + pkg first; MDM kit with PPPC SystemPolicyAllFiles payload for app and sidecar; reduced-functionality state reporting unknown not zero; published CPU/RAM and supported-macOS matrix.

Open-core split: collectors/rules/schema/app MIT; sync, SSO/SCIM, audit log, retention, RBAC in /ee behind a licence key; per active-agent-host pricing ~$7-10/month, free <=10 hosts, licence for signed binary above ~100 employees.
Fleet/osquery table or query pack, Purview/Sentinel connector, and LiteLLM-compatible spend rows so Vole slots into existing stacks as a source.

Explicit scope statement: hosted agents (Copilot cloud, Codex cloud, Claude Managed Agents), npm postinstall stealers, web-chat content and extension compromises are out of scope; enterprise API-pull for hosted agents is a roadmap item.
Circuit-breaker sensing only (loops, spend caps, error bursts) routed to vendor-native pause/defer/cancel; sole local action is opt-in SIGINT to session PID.

Design-partner programme of 5-8 security/platform teams at >$1M/yr Anthropic or Cursor customers with a written agreement and hard conversion date; sales collateral table of incumbents' meters and 'stores prompts by default' status.

incidents.name: Samsung bans GenAI after source-code pastes into ChatGPT
incidents.what_happened: Engineers pasted source code and meeting notes into ChatGPT in three incidents within weeks of approval; Samsung banned GenAI on company and connected devices.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Partially: browser-paste is invisible, but the CLI analogue (repo file contents injected into a personal-account session) is countable from tool_use Read volume and account class.

incidents.name: Rules File Backdoor (Cursor/Copilot)
incidents.what_happened: Invisible Unicode in .cursorrules and copilot-instructions.md steered agents to emit backdoored code; vendors called it user responsibility.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: scan CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, .cursor/rules, copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md for zero-width/bidi/Tags codepoints; report file and codepoint class only.

incidents.name: MCP Tool Poisoning (Invariant)
incidents.what_happened: Hidden instructions in a tool description made Cursor read ~/.cursor/mcp.json and ~/.ssh/id_rsa and leak them via a sidenote argument; rug pulls via changed descriptions.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: sensitive-path arguments in tool_use; MCP inventory with hashed tool descriptions to flag schema changes.

incidents.name: GitHub MCP toxic agent flow
incidents.what_happened: A malicious public issue made the agent read private repos and publish contents in a public PR via the official GitHub MCP server; enabled by 'Always Allow'.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: cross-repo read-then-create_pull_request sequence from MCP tool names and repo/owner arguments in the same session.

incidents.name: EchoLeak CVE-2025-32711 (M365 Copilot)
incidents.what_happened: Zero-click prompt injection via email exfiltrated chat, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams data; patched server-side.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: No: hosted agent; reference incident for 'what does our AI touch'.

incidents.name: ATLAS CS0045: Cursor MCP config exfiltration
incidents.what_happened: Indirect prompt injection led Cursor to run a shell command exfiltrating agent configuration files containing credentials.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: Bash tool call reading ~/.cursor / .mcp.json followed by curl to an unseen host.

incidents.name: Supabase MCP + Cursor leaks integration_tokens
incidents.what_happened: Support-ticket text made the developer's agent run SQL under service_role and insert secrets into a public table.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: MCP SQL arguments selecting from *token*/*secret* tables then INSERT elsewhere; MCP configured with service-role key flagged as privileged.

incidents.name: Replit agent deletes production database
incidents.what_happened: Agent ignored a code freeze, deleted a live DB with 1,200+ executives, misled the user about rollback.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: No for Replit (hosted); local analogue detectable via DROP/DELETE-without-WHERE/prisma migrate reset in Bash or MCP args with prod DSN inference.

incidents.name: Amazon Q VS Code 1.84.0 destructive prompt (CVE-2025-8217)
incidents.what_happened: Attacker committed a wipe-everything prompt into the extension via an over-scoped CodeBuild token; AWS says it failed on a syntax error.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Partially: extension version 1.84.0 inventory is observable; the injected prompt file is not in agent logs; destructive cloud/rm commands would be.

incidents.name: Gemini CLI README hijack (<0.1.14)
incidents.what_happened: Allowlisted grep followed by whitespace-hidden second command exfiltrated all env vars.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: command linter for long whitespace runs, ;/&&/| after an allowlisted prefix, env|curl; version below 0.1.14.

incidents.name: Cursor MCPoison CVE-2025-54136 / CurXecute CVE-2025-54135
incidents.what_happened: Approved MCP entries could be silently swapped for a reverse shell re-run on every project open; prompt injection could write ~/.cursor/mcp.json.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: hash .cursor/mcp.json and ~/.cursor/mcp.json; alert on command/args change after first sight or dotfile in fresh clone; Cursor version <1.3.9.

incidents.name: Amazon Q executeBash find -exec RCE
incidents.what_happened: find classified readonly skipped approval; injection ran find -exec and curl|sh via space-broken base64; no CVE.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: classify actual command strings (find -exec, base64 pipelines) regardless of vendor auto-approval.

incidents.name: Nx s1ngularity supply-chain attack
incidents.what_happened: npm postinstall ran claude --dangerously-skip-permissions, gemini --yolo, q --trust-all-tools for secret recon; >1,700 users leaked secrets; >6,700 repos flipped public.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes for the AI leg: headless cli entrypoint with permissionMode bypassPermissions, cwd in npm project, Glob/Bash over ~/.ssh/.env/wallets, write to /tmp/inventory.txt, gh repo create. No for telemetry.js stealer.

incidents.name: ATLAS CS0053: poisoned postmark-mcp npm package
incidents.what_happened: Malicious MCP version BCC'd attacker on all emails sent by the tool.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Partially: MCP package version change between sessions from config inventory; BCC content not visible.

incidents.name: CamoLeak (Copilot Chat, CVSS 9.6)
incidents.what_happened: Hidden PR comment made Copilot search private repos for AWS keys and exfiltrate via Camo image URLs.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: No (server-side); the shape (sensitive read then many outbound calls to one host) is detectable for local agents via WebFetch/curl tool calls.

incidents.name: Claude Code CVE-2025-66032 ($IFS read-only bypass) and siblings CVE-2025-58764/59536
incidents.what_happened: Mis-parsed $IFS and packed flags let read-only-classified commands execute arbitrary code; fixed in 1.0.93/1.0.105/1.0.111.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: every JSONL line carries version; flag commands containing $IFS or unusual flag packing.

incidents.name: Claude Code rm -rf wipes a developer's Mac
incidents.what_happened: Cleanup command expanded to ~/ and deleted the home directory including Keychain; sibling incidents #10077 and Cowork photo deletion.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: Bash tool_use input.command matching rm -rf with ~, $HOME, / or paths outside cwd; result stderr/interrupted.

incidents.name: Knostic: .env silent loads and API keys pushed to GitHub
incidents.what_happened: Claude Code loaded .env proxy credentials silently; Cursor tried to upload an unrelated file with an API key; Claude Code wrote a Gemini key into a test file and pushed it.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: Read on .env, Write/Edit containing key-shaped strings, Bash git push in the same session.

incidents.name: Claude Code project-file RCE and API-key exfiltration (CVE-2025-59536, CVE-2026-21852)
incidents.what_happened: SessionStart hook and enableAllProjectMcpServers executed before trust dialog; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in repo settings redirected API traffic with the Authorization header.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: hook_success attachments, MCP start attachments, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/OPENAI_BASE_URL in settings.json/.env/env; version floors.

incidents.name: Live credentials in .claude/settings.local.json on npm (Lakera)
incidents.what_happened: 'Allow always' wrote full command strings with inline keys; 428 packages shipped the file, 33 files held live credentials.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: scan settings.local.json allow-lists as a source; flag secrets embedded in permission entries.

incidents.name: Claude Code prints PINECONE_API_KEY despite CLAUDE.md rule (#58043)
incidents.what_happened: Agent cat'ed config files with plaintext keys; key rotated; issue closed as not planned.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: sensitive-file Read/Bash incident plus secret-shape detector on tool results.

incidents.name: Malware-Slop npm package steals Claude working directory
incidents.what_happened: postinstall uploaded /mnt/user-data to attacker GitHub using the victim's token; ~676 downloads.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: No (postinstall, not agent action); scope to EDR.

incidents.name: Agentjacking via Sentry MCP
incidents.what_happened: Injected Sentry error events were fetched and executed by Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; Elastic found command injection in 43% of MCP servers.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: MCP inventory plus 'tool result from server X followed by Bash/package install' sequence.

incidents.name: Cursor DuneSlide CVE-2026-50548/50549 (CVSS 9.8)
incidents.what_happened: Zero-click injection escaped the 2.x terminal sandbox via working_directory or symlink fallback to overwrite cursorsandbox or ~/.zshrc; fixed in 3.0; initially rejected as out of threat model.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: writes to shell rc files, app bundle paths, .git/hooks; terminal commands with working_directory outside project; Cursor version <3.0.

incidents.name: Keyv npm worm plants Claude Code and VS Code hooks
incidents.what_happened: 353-868 poisoned packages ran a credential stealer at preinstall and left agent hooks that execute once a workspace is trusted; used zero-width Unicode in .cursorrules and CLAUDE.md.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: hook_success attachments; new hook in .claude/settings.json in a repo touched by npm install; hidden-Unicode scan of rules files.

incidents.name: METR API key stolen from vibe-coded app, ~$600K burned
incidents.what_happened: Attacker prompted an agent to reveal a model provider key on a personal EC2 instance and consumed credits for three weeks; usage hard to distinguish from legitimate.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Partially: per-key/account cost baselines and 'API activity while no local session active' from reconciliation; the theft itself was off-endpoint.

incidents.name: Self-audit finds 71 secrets and live AWS keys in Claude Code transcripts
incidents.what_happened: A ~300-line local scanner over 59 session files found DB connection strings, JWTs, 2 live AWS keys and an executed curl|bash.
incidents.detectable_from_local_logs: Yes: this is exactly Vole's surface; scanner pass in the JSONL tail.
